questions.q: In the troubleshooting scenario, what is the first thing to check when an invoice is missing from the General Ledger?
options: Immediately delete and recreate the supplier record
Whether a subledger journal entry exists at all for that transaction, using the Review Journal Entries page
Whether the ledger's currency has changed
Whether the Chart of Accounts has the correct number of segments
questions.explain: The first diagnostic step is confirming whether a subledger journal entry exists; if not, the problem is upstream of GL entirely.

questions.q: If Create Accounting errored on the invoice because its freight category had no matching account rule condition, what category of problem is this?
options: A currency conversion error
An incomplete rule, specifically a missing fallback condition on an account rule, as covered in lesson 18
A problem with the ledger's calendar
A problem that has nothing to do with account rules
questions.explain: A rule with no condition matching the transaction's actual data is an incomplete-rule error, the same category covered in the errors and corrections lesson.

questions.q: If a subledger journal entry exists but shows status "Draft," what does that explain about its absence from the GL?
options: Nothing; Draft status has no bearing on whether an entry reaches GL
Draft entries cannot be transferred to the General Ledger under any circumstance, so Final mode simply hasn't run yet
Draft entries are always errors that must be deleted
Draft status means the transaction was entered incorrectly
questions.explain: Because Draft entries are never eligible for transfer, a Draft status alone fully explains why the entry hasn't reached GL yet.

questions.q: If the subledger entry is Final but still missing from the GL, what should be checked next?
options: Whether the supplier's address is correct
Whether Transfer Journal Entries to GL has run since the entry went Final, and whether journal import successfully created the GL batch
Whether the invoice amount is a round number
Whether the ledger has more than one currency
questions.explain: Once an entry is confirmed Final, the next checks are the transfer process and journal import, as covered in lessons 19 and 20.

questions.q: According to the lesson's resolution, since the root cause was a missing condition on the Freight account rule, what is the correct fix?
options: Manually re-enter the invoice as a new transaction with no rule change
Delete the Freight account rule entirely with no replacement
Copy the account rule (per the copy-first discipline), add a condition or fallback for International freight, then re-run Draft to confirm before Final
Ignore the issue since it only affected one invoice
questions.explain: Because the problem traces to the rule itself, the fix follows the copy-first discipline and the Draft-then-Final verification pattern covered earlier in the course.
